sources.claim: RAG combines a seq2seq model with a dense vector index of Wikipedia via a neural retriever (Lewis et al., 2020)
RAG definition: retrieve from knowledge base, pass into context window; quality depends on retrieved data
pgvector: Postgres extension; <=> is cosine distance; HNSW and IVFFlat indexes; exact search by default, approximate index trades recall for speed
HNSW is an approximate nearest neighbour algorithm using multi-layer proximity graphs (Malkov & Yashunin)
Context window = all text model can reference incl. its response; working memory, not training data
Context window = prompt plus generated output combined; token counts and limits vary by model
Tokens may be words, subwords, characters or bytes; counts depend on model and language
Temperature controls randomness; temperature 0 is not fully deterministic
Fine-tuning = further training a pretrained model on additional data
Fine-tuning complements prompting; evals systematically measure performance
Embedding is a vector of floats; cosine similarity recommended for comparing embeddings
Hallucination: models generate false or inconsistent text; mitigations reduce but do not eliminate it
Survey of hallucination in NLG (Ji et al.)
Tool use: model returns a structured call, application executes it and returns tool_result
Evals: define measurable success criteria and automated test cases
Guardrails: input screening, validation, treating retrieved/tool content as untrusted (prompt injection)
Chunking documents, embedding chunks, semantic search; chunks can lack context
Model inputs are called prompts; prompting = providing instructions or examples
Cosine similarity = L2-normalised dot product = cosine of the angle between vectors

scenes.beat: Group 1: talking to the model (items 1-5, reveal one by one, then hold)
on_screen_text: Talking to the model
1. Token: a chunk of text the model reads
2. Context window: max tokens per request, output included
3. Prompt: the instructions and data you send
4. Temperature: controls randomness; 0 can still vary
5. Tool calling: model emits a call; app or API runs it

nodes.sublabel: model emits a call; app or API runs it

on_screen_text: Finding the right data
6. Chunking: split docs into retrievable pieces
7. Embedding: a vector of numbers for meaning
8. Cosine similarity: how closely two vectors align
9. Vector index: structure for fast similarity search
10. ANN search: approximate; trades recall for speed
Making answers reliable
11. RAG: retrieve relevant data, then generate
12. Fine-tuning: further train a model on your own data
13. Hallucination: output that is false or unsupported
14. Evals: repeatable tests of output quality
15. Guardrails: checks on inputs and outputs
